terms.gloss: the shade of a dead person
terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor.; in prose after Augustus
evidence: Hor. C. 4.7.16: pulvis et umbra sumus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The shade of the dead, as in the underworld; Lewis & Short marks this sense as poetic and post-Augustan. Its first sense is “shadow, shade”.

evidence: Plaut. Capt. 3.4.66: larvae stimulant virum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The frightening ghost of comedy and folk belief; Plautus uses it as an insult too (see jerk).

sources: Lewis & Short: umbra
Lewis & Short: larva
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 321.
